articles.title: DIIs book profits in longest selling streak in 4 years
articles.summary: Mumbai: Their roles have decidedly reversed.For years, domestic funds have provided the backstop against exiting foreigners, lifting the share of local stock ownership to a record and preventing a rout of Indian risk assetsOver the past fortnight, however, as foreign funds have come flooding in, domestic institutional investors (DII) have sought to book the profit of patience.Mutual funds, banks, insurers and retirement funds have turned net sellers over the past nine sessions, marking their longest selling streak in four years.135785472Their exits coincide with the sharpest rally in Indian benchmark indices in years - and the meltdown of AI-themed trades in eastern Asia.Data from the NSE showed that DIIs sold equities worth over ₹47,662 crore between October 30 and November 12, marking their longest selling streak since November 2022 when DIIs sold for 10 straight sessions.Read more: New SIP registrations fall 20%, stoppage ratio climbs to 116% in October after 5-month decline If the trend continues, November could become the first month of net selling by DIIs since July 2023, when they offloaded around ₹2,700 crore. It could also mark their steepest monthly selling since November 2020, when they sold equities worth around ₹48,000 crore.Read more: Meesho block deal: SoftBank-backed entity likely to sell 1% stake worth Rs 1,174 croreNilesh Shah, managing director, Kotak Mahindra AMC, said the bulk of the selling is likely coming from profit-booking and portfolio rebalancing by Multi-Asset Allocation Funds (MAFs), Balanced Advantage Funds (BAFs), insurance companies and pension funds. The market rally has pushed up their equity exposure, prompting them to book profits to maintain their targeted asset allocation. Arbitrage funds have also contributed to the selling, albeit to a smaller extent, by exploiting reverse arbitrage opportunities in mid-cap stocks, where futures are trading at a discount to the cash market, prompting funds to sell shares and buy futures, Shah added.The DII selling comes even as foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have returned to Indian equities. Since the beginning of November, the Sensex and Nifty have gained nearly 10% each, while the BSE MidCap 150 and BSE SmallCap 250 indices have advanced around 8% each. FPIs have invested around $8 billion in Indian equities since mid-October, amid a correction in AI-related stocks globally and a decline in crude oil prices.Despite the recent selling, DIIs have remained a key source of support for the market through the year. Akshat Garg, AVP - Research & Product at Choice Wealth, said DIIs had been net buyers of over ₹6.5 lakh crore in 2026, supported by steady SIP and insurance inflows through market corrections. Following the sharp recovery, they are now trimming exposure to richly valued pockets, raising cash and allowing returning foreign investors to take on the role of marginal buyers.

articles.summary: US stocks closed lower on Thursday, as a drop in Nvidia shares after CEO Jensen Huang's exit outweighed gains in energy shares.The chip company's shares fell but were well off the day's lowest level after earlier dropping nearly 12%. Retail investors bought Nvidia shares worth about $111 million in the first half hour of trading, the biggest opening bid on record for the stock, according to data from Vanda Analytics.The S&P 500 lost 25.99 points, or 0.34%, to end at 7,593.39 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 102.44 points, or 0.40%, to 25,363.75. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 190.29 points, or 0.36%, to 52,296.20. The S&P 500 energy index gained about 2%, making it the best performer among the benchmark’s 11 major sectors. Crude prices rose after President Donald Trump wrote on social media that the US did not need a deal with Iran.AI-linked stocks fell globally after Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. AI cloud company Nebius tumbled nearly 18% following its quarterly results and outlook.However, Nvidia rivals and other major technology companies, including Broadcom, Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet and Amazon, advanced and provided the biggest support to the S&P 500.Stocks have been volatile in recent days as sweeping Democratic victories in the US midterm elections fueled concerns about tighter AI regulation. Uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership has also pressured one of the main drivers of the current bull market.Also Read | US stocks: Nvidia shares plunge 13% after Jensen Huang quits as CEO; Colette Kress named interim chief“Right now, the market is selling AI stocks and tech stocks and buying safe stuff, just like it did in the first halo trade in January and February of this year, but it will flip back,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St. Louis.“That’s the tug of war the market is doing right now. It’s concerns about deceleration versus just pointing out that the absolute valuation and growth rates are still pretty compelling.”Nvidia’s financing ties face scrutinyHuang’s departure is expected to intensify scrutiny of AI companies with close financial ties to Nvidia.The chipmaker has backed several businesses, including some of its customers, through financing arrangements that investors are reassessing following the leadership change.Also Read | Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit raises fears over the future of AI financing“Nvidia is the circular-funder-in-chief; they’re the biggest by far at this point, and I assume that activity will moderate,” Ellerbroek said.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 0.5% after gaining 17.2% over the previous four sessions. CoreWeave dropped about 7%, while shares of data-center companies IREN and Applied Digital also declined.Investors await inflation dataInvestors are looking to Friday’s Producer Price Index for further indications about inflation after consumer prices rose more than expected earlier in the week.Markets are fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate increase of at least 25 basis points in December, with a 15% probability of a larger 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Comments from several Fed officials this week suggested the central bank could consider a more aggressive path of rate increases as price pressures intensify.Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said Thursday that she did not believe the central bank needed to shift to larger rate increases to control inflation. articles.title: Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit raises fears over the future of AI financing
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday raised concerns not only about the future of the multitrillion-dollar chipmaker but also about its willingness and ability to continue financing the artificial intelligence boom, Reuters reported.Huang’s exit added another pressure point to one of the global market’s most crowded trades. It came after Nvidia’s board met late Wednesday to consider the longtime CEO’s future following reports of two extramarital affairs.Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a permanent successor, the company said in a statement.Investors initially sold Nvidia shares and stocks linked to the company, including data-centre operator CoreWeave and South Korea’s Naver. Shares of chipmaking rivals Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices advanced.Chinese graphics-processing-unit makers also rallied on expectations that Nvidia’s leadership upheaval could help local suppliers gain market share. Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon each surged nearly 10%.Nvidia shares fell 13%, while Nasdaq 100 futures declined 0.6%.The broader concern is that Nvidia could scale back its strategy of financing data centres under new leadership, potentially slowing investment across the AI industry.Also Read | Anthropic IPO: Can Indian investors apply for Claude maker's $64 billion share sale? Check rules“Nvidia has been called the ‘Bank of AI’. They’ll sell you the chips and loan you the money. If they have to take a step back because of what’s going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That’s an open question,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey, according to Reuters.Nvidia has been the flagship stock of the AI revolution. Its technological lead and surging sales have driven its share price up about 900% in the four years since the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT helped usher in the generative-AI era.The company has also emerged as a major financier of the industry, investing billions of dollars in customers through equity stakes and other financial commitments as it anticipates growing demand for increasingly powerful chips.“Nvidia’s credit support is what makes much of this debt finance-able across the AI hyperscaler deal front,” said Christopher Brown, senior vice president, investments, at Synovus Securities. “Lenders will ask what happens to that support if Nvidia’s leadership or regulatory standing is impaired, and Nvidia’s own willingness to extend more guarantees may be constrained.”Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into Huang after reports that he had an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy. A separate report involving another alleged affair emerged before Wednesday’s board meeting.Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told Reuters that Nvidia’s revenue was unlikely to fall suddenly following Huang’s departure. The greater concern, he said, was the company’s long-term direction because of Huang’s central role in shaping its computing strategy.“Replacing that strategic vision ... is an enormous challenge,” Boloor said.Nvidia’s departure reverberates across AI stocksHuang’s exit creates a leadership vacuum at the roughly $4 trillion company he co-founded and built over more than three decades. Nvidia has become the leading supplier of AI chips and a focal point of the technology rivalry between the United States and China.Asian chip stocks, which had rallied alongside Nvidia during the AI spending boom but recently came under pressure from concerns about financing costs and demand, also declined.Nvidia disclosed $164.5 billion in financial commitments in its latest earnings report. These included an obligation of up to $105 billion tied to an OpenAI data centre in Ohio and more than $50 billion in lease and capacity guarantees.In August, Nvidia said it had partnered with six major financial institutions, including Apollo, BlackRock and Blackstone, to establish computing-finance platforms seeking more than $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Huang said the company could backstop as much as $125 billion, or 25% of the potential deals.“The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raise the question of whether that created more stability or more fragility,” Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers, told Reuters.Nvidia is also an investor in Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot. Anthropic’s initial public offering this month is expected to test investor demand for AI-related assets.CoreWeave shares fell more than 7.5% in premarket trading after surging Wednesday on upbeat earnings. Naver, in which Nvidia invested $1 billion by financing a data-centre expansion, dropped 6%.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: What Nvidia said after CEO’s shocking exit
articles.summary: In a move that would certainly send shockwaves through the tech world, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company as president, chief executive officer (CEO) and a member of the company's board of directors, with immediate effect on Thursday.Meanwhile, Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been appointed as interim chief executive officer as the chip giant begins a search for a permanent successor.Nvidia's board said it will consider both internal and external candidates for the position. Kress will continue to serve as the company's executive vice president and CFO while serving as interim CEO until a permanent successor is appointed.Also Read | Jensen Huang quits as Nvidia CEO amid affair scandal; AI chip giant names Colette Kress interim chiefThe company did not disclose a reason for Huang's resignation in its announcement.Kress has served as Nvidia's executive vice president and CFO since joining the company in September 2013. During her tenure, she has led the company's finance organisation and played a key role in Nvidia's growth and evolution.Before joining Nvidia, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.What Nvidia's board saidHarvey C. Jones, who has been appointed Nvidia's first-ever chair of the board, said Kress has helped lead the company through a period of “extraordinary growth” and has a deep understanding of its business, customers, operations and financial position.The board said it has “full confidence” in Kress and the leadership team and expects Nvidia's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said.She added that Nvidia would continue advancing its work in accelerated computing and AI while focusing on customers, partners, developers and shareholders.Also Read | Jensen Huang and the Chinese spy honeytrap: How does China allegedly use this strategy to gather sensitive US information?Jensen Huang's Nvidia legacyThe board said Huang's contributions to Nvidia were “profound” and described the company as one of the world's most consequential technology companies.“The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” Nvidia said.Huang founded Nvidia and has led the company for 33 years, overseeing its transformation into a dominant player in accelerated computing and AI.A private affair, a very public exitHuang, 63, co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has been at the helm of the company for more than three decades. During that time, he transformed Nvidia from a graphics chipmaker into one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global artificial intelligence boom. His departure marks a major change for the company and the semiconductor industry.Huang's exit comes amid a controversy involving Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, whom US intelligence agencies suspect of gathering information for Beijing. Huang admitted to having an extramarital relationship with her and apologised to his wife, children and Nvidia employees.The revelations prompted Nvidia's board to launch an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company, however, said its board had no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia's confidential information had been compromised. The affair finally cost Huang to step down from his position from the company.

articles.title: Kimberly Powell: Nvidia career in spotlight
articles.summary: Kimberly Powell has spent 18 years at Nvidia, moving from medical imaging to some of the company's biggest healthcare AI projects, including genomics and drug discovery. But the 48-year-old vice president is now in the headlines for a different reason.The New York Times reported on November 11 that she had an intimate relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, 63, who is her direct boss. The report cited five people who worked at the company and said the two were seen being affectionate in a video recorded at a San Jose hotel during an Nvidia conference in March. Powell is married, the newspaper reported.When the Times asked Huang about his relationship with Powell, he reportedly replied, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly," before ending the call. Powell and Nvidia had not responded to Business Insider's requests for comment as of November 12. Neither has confirmed the reported relationship.The report comes as Nvidia is already dealing with another controversy involving Huang. The CEO recently told employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without naming anyone.Separately, the company's board has been examining whether a technology executive with alleged links to Chinese intelligence targeted Huang. That case involves Alice Huang, not Kimberly Powell. Together, the developments have put the company's leadership, internal policies and board oversight under fresh scrutiny.Who is Kimberly Powell and what is her role at Nvidia?Powell is one of Nvidia's senior executives responsible for taking its AI computing technology beyond conventional chip applications. Her current role covers healthcare and life sciences, two areas where Nvidia wants to expand the use of accelerated computing and artificial intelligence.        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Yahoo Finance (@yahoofinance)She joined Nvidia in 2008 as a director. Her initial responsibility was to establish Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) as computing accelerators for medical imaging equipment.Before joining Nvidia, Powell worked in hardware engineering and product management at Planar Systems, where she focused on diagnostic imaging systems. She holds a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, with a concentration in computer engineering, from Northeastern University.Her entry into Nvidia was not the result of a conventional executive recruitment process. On an August 2026 episode of the Lifers podcast, she explained that she had contacted Nvidia to discuss its computing technology. The company subsequently recognised its potential applications in healthcare and approached her about joining.She described the opportunity as a "dream come true."Powell's responsibilities grew over the years. Her LinkedIn profile says she became a senior director in 2016, leading an AI-focused business development team. In 2017, she was promoted to vice president of healthcare.When she joined in 2008, one of the main opportunities was using GPUs to process medical images. Medical imaging systems generate large volumes of data, and GPUs can process many calculations simultaneously. This makes them useful for applications such as analysing CT scans, MRI images and other diagnostic images.Over time, Nvidia expanded this approach into other parts of healthcare.Its medical imaging platform, MONAI, provides tools for developing AI applications that analyse medical images. Its BioNeMo platform supports AI research in biology and drug discovery. Parabricks uses accelerated computing to process genomic data.Powell's role has therefore expanded from promoting GPUs for imaging equipment to developing a wider computing and software ecosystem for healthcare companies, hospitals and pharmaceutical researchers.According to her profile on the Milken Institute's website, she also oversees the global strategy and commercial expansion of these platforms.Kimberly Powell report and Alice Huang investigationThe Powell report is the second major development involving Huang's personal relationships to emerge during Nvidia's current leadership crisis. But the two cases concern different women and different allegations.The first involves Alice Huang, a technology executive associated with Megaspeed. The New York Times previously reported that US officials believed she might have been recruited by the Chinese government to gather information about Nvidia.The allegations have raised national security questions because Nvidia makes some of the world's most advanced AI chips, which are subject to US export restrictions on sales to China.Nvidia's board launched an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The company has also faced scrutiny over its relationship with Alice Huang and the circumstances surrounding the alleged intelligence operation.The issue has also reached Congress. Republican lawmakers have sought a closed-door briefing from Huang on his relationship with Alice Huang and the national security concerns surrounding Nvidia's business in China.On November 11, Reuters reported that Nvidia's board had met to consider whether Huang should be removed as CEO. The Wall Street Journal separately reported that the board was preparing to oust him.Nvidia has 11 board members, including Huang. Under the company's bylaws, a majority of directors can remove him, with or without cause. All directors other than Huang are considered independent.As of November 12, no final removal decision had been publicly announced.Reuters also reported that there was no obvious successor if Huang were removed. However, the stock fell more than 8% in extended trading after reports that the board was considering Huang's future.Reuters reported that Nvidia shares also fell around 7% in early Frankfurt trading on November 12. articles.title: India’s Russian fossil fuel imports hit record
articles.summary: India was the second-largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels in October, purchasing hydrocarbons worth €6.4 billion, according to a monthly analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA). It was India’s highest monthly total in data going back to January 2022.Crude oil accounted for 91% of India’s purchases at €5.8 billion. Coal imports were worth €333 million, while oil products accounted for €232 million.Indian refineries raise Russian crude purchasesIndia’s imports of Russian crude oil rose 10% from September. Imports increased at all three of the country’s largest importing refineries—Vadinar, Jamnagar and Paradip.Imports at Vadinar rose 12% month-on-month, while Jamnagar and Paradip recorded increases of 22% and 28%, respectively. The rise made Jamnagar the biggest importer of seaborne Russian crude in October.Refineries in India, Turkiye and Brunei that use Russian crude exported oil products worth €1.6 billion to countries imposing sanctions in October. The destinations included the European Union, Australia, the US and New Zealand.Ten of the 12 shipments of oil products from refineries processing Russian crude that reached EU ports in October departed from India’s Jamnagar refinery. The remaining two shipments came from Turkiye’s STAR refinery.CREA estimated that €389 million worth of the oil products exported by these refineries were made from Russian crude. Exports from the refineries to sanctioning countries rose 21% in volume terms from September.Russia’s fossil fuel earnings reach four-year highChina remained the largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels, purchasing €10.7 billion worth of hydrocarbons in October. The European Union was the third-largest buyer at €2.2 billion, followed by Turkiye at €1.1 billion and South Korea at €488 million.Russia’s total fossil fuel export revenues rose 14% month-on-month to €754 million per day in October, the highest monthly level since December 2022. Export volumes remained broadly unchanged.Crude oil export revenues rose 19% to €449 million per day, with seaborne crude earnings increasing 23% to €352 million per day. CREA said this was the highest monthly level recorded since its data series began in January 2022.The report said higher global oil prices, linked to the energy crisis around the Strait of Hormuz, helped increase Russia’s fossil fuel earnings. Russia’s Urals crude averaged $101.70 a barrel in October, more than twice the EU and UK price cap of $44.10 a barrel.CREA also said that 60% of Russia’s seaborne oil was transported by sanctioned “shadow” tankers in October. Another 37% was carried by tankers owned or insured in G7 countries and their partners.A crude oil price cap of $30 a barrel, if fully enforced, would have reduced Russia’s seaborne crude oil export revenues by 21%, or €2.2 billion, in October, CREA said. A lower cap on crude and oil products together could have reduced Russia’s total seaborne oil export revenues by 25%, or €3.4 billion.

articles.title: US stock market selloff: Four indicators suggest correction may not be over
articles.summary: The recent selloff in US stocks has left investors searching for signs of a market bottom, but four key indicators suggest it may be too early to declare the correction over, according to a Reuters analysis.Technology and artificial intelligence-related stocks have fallen around 10% from their recent peaks after the Nasdaq-100 hit a record high in early October. While shares have stabilised somewhat, investor positioning, options activity and technical indicators continue to signal caution.Read more: Chinese yuan edges higher, but stronger dollar caps gains Technology positioning shows signs of easingAccording to Deutsche Bank data cited by Reuters, investors have reduced exposure to technology stocks since late September, shifting towards other sectors. The latest selloff pushed tech positioning below levels recorded during the April 2025 tariff-related market turmoil.Deutsche Bank strategist Parag Thatte said the decline appeared to be driven by investors unwinding crowded positions. He added that positioning levels could create conditions for a technology sector rebound.Stock correlations offer some reliefAnother relatively positive signal is the limited increase in expected stock correlations. Barclays strategists noted that three-month realised correlation among the 50 largest S&P 500 companies fell to a record low in late September.Although expectations for correlations increased during last week's selloff, the rise remained modest. Rocky Fishman, founder of Asym Research, said this suggested investors viewed the decline as a sector-specific correction rather than a broader economic downturn, Reuters reported.Read more: South Korean shares rise as tech stocks rebound on Wall StreetOptions activity presents a mixed pictureRetail investors had purchased call options on individual stocks in record volumes this year, helping support the AI rally. However, that trend reversed sharply last week.According to Carrick Lane data, retail call buying in AI stocks dropped significantly, contributing to the post-election selloff.The shift has reduced excessive bullish positioning, but options indicators have not weakened enough to provide a strong buying signal.Technical indicators remain cautiousTechnical signals continue to suggest that the market may not have reached its bottom. Mark Newton, head of technical strategy at Fundstrat Global Advisors, said the rebound in the Invesco QQQ ETF, which tracks the Nasdaq-100, had stalled below its downward trend line.Weak short-term momentum and the absence of a DeMark exhaustion signal suggest US stocks could remain volatile for another couple of weeks, Newton said.Overall, while reduced technology exposure and relatively stable stock correlations offer some encouragement, options positioning and technical trends suggest investors should remain cautious before calling an end to the market correction.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. articles.summary: Shares of Ola Electric Mobility jumped more than 7% on Thursday ahead of the EV scooter-maker’s Q2 earnings announcement. The moves are aimed to promote electric mobility, reducing dependence on fossil fuels, and taking into account the prevailing market prices and lifecycle costs of vehicles."Going forward, Ministries and Departments shall ordinarily procure Electric Vehicles (EVs) at the time of condemnation or replacement of their existing ICE staff cars. articles.title: Oil below $92 amid hopes of peace talks
articles.summary: Oil prices edged lower by more than $1 on Thursday as investors increasingly hopes for peace talks to resolve the Middle East conflict as well as the much-longer lasting Russia-Ukraine war.Brent crude futures fell more than $1 to trade below $92 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures also lost over $1 to trade below $86 per barrel on Thursday morning. This comes after Brent crude rose over 1% on Wednesday after hitting two-month lows in the previous day.Russian and Ukrainian negotiators have agreed to a major prisoner exchange during their peace talks held over two days in Abu Dhabi, although US mediators said differences remained on other major issues, including territory. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country hoped to achieve concrete results on resolving the war this year.Also read | India's battered rupee finds an unlikely rescue party in cheaper oil and Wall Street's AI routBack in the Middle East, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the government will not allow even a single particle of enriched nuclear material to leave Iran and there will be consequences if the US launches new strikes. The US meanwhile has said that nuclear issues must be part of any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the eight-month-old war, while US officials downplayed the need for further military strikes.Meanwhile, OPEC+ crude oil production jumped in October, driven by a sharp increase in output from Saudi Arabia despite continued disruption to shipments through the Hormuz Strait. US crude stocks jumped by 9 million barrels in the latest week, Reuters quoted market sources as saying, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.Where are oil prices heading for?While oil prices have dropped from their multi decade highs which they hit earlier this year, analysts remain cautious amid the seesaw political game in the Middle East.
